edges.description: Activated circulating memory B cells, plasmablasts, and T-helper subsets traffic to the biliary tree and establish IgG4-rich lymphoplasmacytic ductal infiltration.
Shared systemic IgG4-related adaptive immune activation frequently involves the pancreas concomitantly as type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis.
Persistent transmural lymphoplasmacytic infiltration drives storiform fibrogenesis, duct-wall thickening, and luminal stenosis.
Immune-mediated transmural inflammation of intrahepatic and extrahepatic ducts manifests clinically as IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis.
Diffuse periductal fibrosis and progressive ductal stenosis produce the characteristic biliary strictures of sclerosing cholangitis.
Fibrostenotic narrowing of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts impairs bile outflow, causing biochemical and clinical cholestasis.
Biliary stricture and impaired conjugated bilirubin excretion produce obstructive jaundice.
Cholestatic retention of pruritogenic biliary solutes downstream of bile duct stenosis causes cholestatic pruritus.
Biliary stricture, ductal hypertension, and pancreatobiliary fibroinflammation cause symptomatic abdominal pain.
Chronic biliary obstruction, cholestasis, and systemic fibroinflammatory activity frequently present with unintentional weight loss mimicking hepatobiliary malignancy.

evidence.snippet: Insights into the genetic and immunological features of the disease have increased over the past decade, with an emphasis on HLAs, T cells, circulating memory B cells and plasmablasts, chemokine-mediated trafficking, as well as the role of the innate immune system.

nodes.description: Fibroinflammatory remodeling around affected bile ducts narrows the duct lumen and causes cholestasis, biliary obstruction, and downstream liver injury.

evidence.reference_title: IgG4-Related Sclerosing Cholangitis and Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
evidence.snippet: Sclerosing cholangitis (SC) is defined as a condition with progressive stenosis and destruction of the bile ducts due to diffuse inflammation and fibrosis and currently includes three categories: primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), secondary cholangitis, and IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis (IgG4-SC).
These diseases can present with biliary strictures and/or mass lesions, making them difficult to differentiate from primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) or other hepatobiliary malignancies.

nodes.description: Endoscopic decompression is used selectively for clinically significant obstructive jaundice, acute cholangitis, or dominant biliary strictures; stents should be removed promptly when strictures improve after corticosteroids.
